sections.heading: Direct Builder Specs and P2P Bid Configuration
sections.summary: Agreement to remove per-builder P2P bid boosting/min-bid config; PRs to be implemented by clients before merging.
sections.body:
- Three open PRs cover the builder spec updates, Beacon API changes, and Key Manager API for Gloas direct builders.
  - Key Manager API (PR #88) makes auction configuration programmatic, avoiding large error-prone configs.
  - Beacon API (PR #630) sends enough info from the Validator client to the Beacon node to facilitate the auction.
  - Builder spec PR (#165) mostly clarifies existing behavior and brings it up to standard after Brath's departure.
- Current specs allow per-builder boost factor and min-bid for P2P bids, but this does not work deterministically because P2P gossip only propagates the highest bid by actual `bid.value`, not by any boosted factor.
  - Nico Flaig (Lodestar) argued the per-builder P2P config produces random outcomes and is bad design.
- Decision: remove per-builder P2P bid boosting and min-bid config from the specs.
  - No client team wanted to keep per-builder P2P preferences.
  - Prysm deferred to Nico and Terence but was fine with removal.
  - Eitan (Lighthouse) explicitly did not want per-builder P2P config.
- Global boost factor (e.g., 10% local payload boost) remains; only per-builder P2P configuration is removed.
- Action item: Jason Vranek to update the PRs today to remove per-builder P2P bid config.
- Agreement: PRs will not be merged yet; clients will implement first, test on devnet, and then merge.
  - No client besides Lodestar currently runs spec tests on the API, so early merge provides little value.
  - Prysm agreed to this approach as long as current state is signaled as the right direction.

sections.heading: Builder Bids with Insufficient Balance: Ignore vs. Reject
sections.summary: Agreement to keep the insufficient-balance check as IGNORE rather than changing it to REJECT, to avoid losing P2P bid functionality.
sections.body:
- The [consensus spec](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/6afc99391cbe7d01eb8a80e619b4168a052fd084/specs/gloas/p2p-interface.md?plain=1#L975-L977) currently marks bids from builders with insufficient balance as IGNORE.
- Nico initially suggested changing this to REJECT since the check is not timing-dependent and the correct state can always be determined.
- Prysm (potuz) disagreed: clients should not be forced to use a non-head state to validate gossip objects.
  - If a peer forwards a bid built on a non-head parent, the receiving node may not have the correct state to validate the balance check.
  - If changed to REJECT, Prysm would simply ignore all bids not built on head, effectively removing the multi-parent bid functionality that was specifically added.
  - Risk of peer downscoring for a low-stakes gossip validation.
- Nico accepted this rationale and agreed to keep the check as IGNORE.
- No other client objected; decision is to leave the spec unchanged.

sections.heading: Parent Bids at Epoch Boundaries
sections.summary: Lodestar will ignore parent bids at epoch boundaries to avoid double epoch transitions; spec PR from Prysm will formalize removing the shuffling-stability check.
sections.body:
- Lodestar observed on devnet that bids for parent blocks at epoch boundaries cause two epoch transitions, effectively DOSing the node.
  - [Lodestar PR #9756](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9756) ignores parent bids at epoch boundaries to prevent this.
- Prysm (potuz) noted this is not contradictory with Lighthouse's epoch-boundary reorg feature or Prysm's own spec PR that allows such bids.
  - Prysm will have the required state cached if the last block came late, so it can validate those bids.
  - It is fine for Lodestar to ignore them if it doesn't have the data.
- The spec-level change (potuz's PR) removes the `isShufflingStable` check, which is now unnecessary because the look-ahead already ensures shuffling stability.
  - Both Lighthouse and Prysm are already doing this on mainnet.
  - Action item: potuz to add a rationale paragraph to the PR explaining why the check is redundant.

sections.heading: Per-Slot Pool Engine API for Devnet 8
sections.summary: Lighthouse raised concerns about the per-slot Pool Engine API at a prior call; no counter-proposal yet, so teams are asked to review and provide async feedback.
sections.body:
- At the last ACD meeting, the per-slot Pool Engine API was discussed as mandatory for glamsterdam-devnet-8.
- Lighthouse raised design concerns, and the group agreed to revisit the topic at this call.
- No counter-proposal has been submitted; other client teams have already implemented the current proposal.
- Bosul Mun asked all client teams to review the current proposal and share feedback asynchronously.
  - General view is to proceed unless significant objections arise.
